statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 12 of 100 in the low band, thirteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME equity index futures halt that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday is now more than thirty-seven hours old and removes the very price path this score measures; twelve of the twenty-four published forward slots lie inside that closure. Stress holds in the high band at 66, one point above the previous hour, because this hour added escalation confirmation rather than a new transmission channel: a second vessel was reported struck and set alight in the strait, an Iranian official attributed the Qeshm strike to the United States, and the Houthis claimed drones and missiles on the Sharurah base after a projectile wounded two in Jazan. The offsetting diplomatic leg is intact, with GCC and Iraqi foreign ministers due to meet Iran's counterpart in Salalah on Monday on temporary Hormuz shipping lanes. Confidence is 86 on primary-source verification of the index level and day range, VIX, H.15 yields, oil, the seven-day calendar and every published item cited here, held below the very-high band because no live price path is observable during the halt. Tail stays below the block threshold across the whole horizon and reaches the watch band only in the five slots around the scheduled 22:00 UTC restart.
recommendation: Tail sits in the low band, so the deterministic repository mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and this single shared reading applies jointly to NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three observations support it. First, no venue quotes the Nasdaq-100 in twelve of the twenty-four published forward slots: CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, so there is no gap, no failed retracement and no session extreme available to score. Second, the weekend record is severe but is carried in Stress rather than Tail, because Tail measures a pathological price path and no path currently exists to be pathological; the record is also two-sided, with the Salalah meeting on temporary Hormuz shipping lanes set against the vessel strikes and the Yemen exchanges. Third, the one structural checkpoint inside the horizon is the scheduled restart, and the five watch-band slots from 22:00 UTC on Sunday to 03:00 UTC on Monday are published as a narrow evidence-based danger window rather than a broad session-wide shutdown. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this reading.
headline: With CME equity index futures halted since 21:00 UTC on Friday the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX 15.84, while Iranian state media report a commercial vessel struck near Qeshm in the Strait of Hormuz with one dead and four wounded and a second vessel hit and set alight, an Iranian official attributes the strike to the United States, Saudi civil defence reports a Houthi projectile wounding two in Jazan, WTI holds $100.05 after a 9.7 per cent weekly gain, the 10-year closed at 4.975 per cent, and GCC and Iraqi foreign ministers are due to meet Iran's counterpart in Salalah on Monday ahead of Wednesday's FOMC, where roughly 85 to 90 per cent of a 25 basis point increase is priced.
body:
Last observed tape. The Nasdaq-100 closed Friday at 29,368.44, up 0.91 per cent, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 day range and about 4.5 per cent below its 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. VIX fell 11.2 per cent to 15.84 from a 17.71 intraday high. The move was a relief rally that recovered part of the S&P 500's deepest four-day decline since June, with nine of eleven sectors higher, after in-line headline inflation and a sharp pullback in crude. That is two-sided, mean-reverting behaviour rather than one-way structure, which is why the published dominant mode is normal.

Cross-asset state. WTI settled at $100.05, down 2.37 per cent on Friday but up 9.7 per cent on the week, with Brent at $104.61; Friday's pullback followed Iranian state media confirming Tehran would meet Gulf states in Oman on the Strait of Hormuz. The 10-year Treasury closed at 4.975 per cent, and H.15 for 10 September shows the 2-year at 4.56 per cent and the 30-year at 5.37 per cent against an effective federal funds rate of 3.63 per cent, so the curve already embeds a further tightening step. Oil above $100 alongside a recovering equity tape is a conflict rather than an alignment, and conflicting signals raise Stress rather than Tail.

Weekend record. Iranian state media reported a commercial vessel struck near Qeshm Island, about 14 miles from Bandar Abbas, killing one of a ten-member crew and wounding four; a second vessel was reported struck by a projectile with a fire breaking out and the crew evacuated, and the UK Maritime Trade Operations monitor reported a vessel hit while transiting. The Qeshm governor blamed a terrorist enemy and an Iranian official attributed the strike to the United States; US Central Command had not commented as of publication. Strait throughput is already reported at roughly 90 per cent below pre-conflict levels. In Yemen, Saudi civil defence reported a Houthi projectile in Jazan's al-Tuwal wounding two and damaging a mosque, buildings and vehicles, while the Houthis claimed drones and ballistic missiles against the Sharurah base and exchanges continued around Bab al-Mandeb. Against that, foreign ministers of the GCC states and Iraq are due to meet Iran's counterpart in Salalah on Monday, building on the August Iran-Oman agreement on a temporary route, mine clearing and short-term management of the strait.

Scheduled checkpoints. Wednesday's FOMC decision and projections land at 18:00 UTC with the press conference at 18:30 UTC, preceded the same morning by August Retail Sales at 12:30 UTC. Roughly 85 to 90 per cent of a 25 basis point increase from the 3.50 to 3.75 per cent range is already priced after August core CPI came in at 0.3 per cent month over month and payrolls rose 162,000, so the projections and tone carry the residual risk rather than the decision. The Bank of England follows on Thursday and the Bank of Japan concludes on Friday, which compounds the week's rate-event load.

How this maps. Tail is 12 because the halt removes the observable price path that Tail scores, and because crossing into the block region requires observed persistent one-way structure or several current amplifiers, neither of which a closed market can supply. Stress is 66 because a hiking Fed, oil above $100, a 10-year near 5 per cent and an active regional conflict together describe a genuinely difficult environment. Confidence is 86 on full primary-source verification, capped below the very-high band by the absence of live price discovery. The one bounded checkpoint is the scheduled 22:00 UTC restart, where conditional Tail peaks at 24 in the watch band and still below the block threshold, then decays to 19 by 03:00 UTC on the assumption of orderly two-sided repricing; that assumption is replaced by observed evidence at the next hourly assessment.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 10:00 UTC on 12 September to 09:00 UTC on 13 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The whole window sits inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday. Tail held at 6 for the first nineteen slots, then stepped to 7 at 05:00 UTC, 8 at 06:00, 9 at 07:00, 10 at 08:00 and 11 at 09:00 on 13 September, tracking elapsed time without price discovery rather than any observed structure. Stress traced a shallow U: it eased from 56 to 50 between 10:00 and 17:00 UTC on 12 September as Friday's cash session closed with a relief rally and crude pulled back, then rebuilt to 65 by 08:00 UTC on 13 September as the weekend Hormuz and Yemen record accumulated. Confidence stayed between 85 and 87 throughout. Every slot mapped to EA_ON and green in normal mode, so no lookback hour reached the watch band.
outlookSummary: Twelve of the twenty-four forward slots lie inside the CME weekend closure; the reference contract is scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, this horizon's thirteenth slot. Conditional Tail opens at 12 in the current slot, the only slot describing observed rather than hypothetical conditions, and drifts to 19 by 20:00 UTC as unpriced weekend exposure accumulates. It is capped at 19 through the closure because a halted contract cannot show the one-way structure Tail measures. The restart slot carries the horizon's peak at 24, the top of the watch band and one point below the block threshold, because the first prints must absorb two Hormuz vessel strikes, Iranian attribution of one of them to the United States, Houthi fire into Saudi territory and Monday's Salalah diplomacy simultaneously in thin liquidity. Tail then decays to 19 by 03:00 UTC on the assumption of orderly two-sided price discovery, and the published danger window is deliberately limited to 22:00 UTC Sunday through 03:00 UTC Monday rather than the whole Monday session. Stress stays in the high band in every slot, between 65 and 71, and leads Tail throughout because a hiking Fed, oil above $100, a 10-year near 5 per cent and an active regional conflict describe a difficult environment rather than a path that denies mean reversion. Monday's later slots shift toward positioning into Wednesday's FOMC, where roughly 85 to 90 per cent of a 25 basis point increase is already priced.
